title: I trained a model that turns two generated head pictures into MHR face parameters for the SOMA mesh
author: zjgkkn
selftext:
I trained a model that takes two generated pictures of a head (front and profile) and returns the parameters of the closest matching face for the SOMA mesh (MHR), ready for facial animation.

It runs locally. Download: [https://huggingface.co/zjgkkn/frommhr](https://huggingface.co/zjgkkn/frommhr)

I've seen models that guess MHR body parameters from a video or a picture, but I couldn't find anything like that for the face.

It was trained only on synthetic data: random face parameters are rendered into pictures, and the model learns to recover the parameters from them.

I'm happy with the result: together with procedural texture baking it gives quite decent characters. MHR has limits on children's faces, so children come out worse. For them I have a fallback (not released yet): a model built on Anny's parameters, which outputs the same SOMA mesh.

I'd be glad if anyone finds this useful, and happy to hear any comments!

**How it was made**

\- Made together with Claude Code: it wrote the code and ran the experiments, I made the calls and judged the results.

\- **Data**:no real faces. Each training step draws random MHR heads and random skin and eye pigments, then renders a front and a profile on the fly with a small PyTorch rasteriser: random light, small head turns, blur, noise.

\- **Network**: DINOv2 ViT-S/14 at 518 px on both pictures, plus a small CNN on the eyes (DINOv2's features held no iris colour), then an MLP to 20 shape coefficients and 14 colour sliders.

\- **Loss**: the head is rebuilt from the predicted coefficients and compared with the true one in millimetres, plus the colour difference.

\- **Training**: 6.8 hours on an RTX 3070 Laptop (8 GB). On held-out synthetic heads the error is 0.27 mm on average, against 4.5 mm for the average head.

\- **Children**: we measured that MHR's 20 head directions cover only 74–80% of how a child's head differs from an adult's, and pushing the coefficients further doesn't help: that part just isn't in MHR.

\- **Character pipeline**: front + profile from an image model → frommhr → the head on a rigged SOMA body (size from numbers: sex, age, height, weight) → face texture baked from the pictures. Hair and clothes are separate parts.

comments.author: Nuaua
comments.body: Cool, I've been working on something similar for the body (high res 3D mesh -> Soma rig), I'll try to add this for the face.

replies.author: zjgkkn
replies.body: Hope you will find it useful! i guess there are some solid solutions exists already for image to soma body modality from meta itself.

replies.author: Nuaua
replies.body:
Yeah SAM 3D Body seems decent, but I haven't tried it. I'm not sure how good it is at recovering details. Maybe having a 3D sculpt as input gives a bit more control than an image too. That's how it looks now (with the 3 LODs of SOMA):

https://imgur.com/a/Vj4kAyq

I'm also working on a z-weave style cloth generator to go with it.

replies.author: zjgkkn
replies.body: I'm almost sure it does. i expect that limits are similar to those I'm faced with face recovering. MHR params not flexible enough to create a non realistic body.

replies.author: zjgkkn
replies.body: oh, cloth is my headache for now, it either consumes a ton of tokens or looks super bad...
